method.cost.p1: A-share commission both ways, stamp duty on sells, slippage, and a 5-yuan minimum commission. Signals form on the bar’s close and fill at the next open; what you buy today you can only sell tomorrow (T+1). High-turnover strategies look best gross and fall behind first net.
method.cost.title: 3 · Costs and T+1
method.lead: A good backtest does not make a strategy work. This page lays out how we stop fooling ourselves: walk-forward validation, overfitting checks, costs with T+1, and survivorship bias. Numbers come from one trend_vol validation report.
method.lookahead.p1: A signal may use only data up to the current bar’s close; fills happen on the next bar. Before 15:30 Beijing time, the current day’s bar is off limits (half a session). The same strategy must agree across all three engines within tolerance — otherwise we check the rules first.
method.lookahead.title: Throughout: no look-ahead
method.of.p1: Try 96 parameter sets and one will look good. Under multiple testing, the best Sharpe has to be discounted: the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) accounts for the number of trials and the skew and kurtosis of returns, giving the probability that the Sharpe is not luck.
method.of.p2: PBO (Probability of Backtest Overfitting) uses combinatorially symmetric cross-validation: the probability that the in-sample optimum lands below median out-of-sample. We require DSR > 0.6 and PBO < 0.4, and neighbouring parameters must also work.
method.of.title: 2 · Overfitting checks
method.sb.p1: Backtesting only on stocks that still exist today means knowing in advance who survived. Our universe is built as it stood at the time: delisted and suspended names stay until their last day and exit at the final traded price.
method.sb.p2: The same strategy gains a few points of CAGR and a shallower drawdown once delisted names are dropped. That gain is an illusion.
method.sb.title: 4 · Survivorship bias
method.title: Methodology
method.wf.p1: History is cut into 5 folds. Each fold trains on 46 months (parameter selection) and tests on the next 12, which the training step never sees. The five test windows stitched together form an out-of-sample curve you could actually have had at the time.
method.wf.p2: We look at the out-of-sample Sharpe and its decay relative to in-sample. A 30–50% decay is common; above 60% says the parameters were picked to fit history.
method.wf.title: 1 · Walk-forward validation

usmon.cfg.hint: Each stock is requested at most once per 300 s and requests are at least 10 s apart regardless of this interval; consecutive failures lengthen the wait automatically and rate limiting triggers a 10-minute cooldown; changes apply from the next round.
usmon.q.time_note: All times are US Eastern time (daylight saving handled automatically). Prices are intraday samples, not closing prices, and are never used to recompute strategy signals.
usmon.q.empty: No watched stocks: the US watchlist has no valid symbols (holdings and signals are empty in this version), or monitoring has not started. This is normal, not a fault.
usmon.phase.waiting_session: Waiting for trading hours (US Eastern 09:30–16:00, Mon–Fri)
usmon.phase.cooling_down: Cooling down (requests deferred after a failure or rate limit)
usmon.reason.budget_exhausted: The request budget for this run is used up; start again manually
usmon.reason.quality_error: Three consecutive data-quality failures (possibly a market holiday or stale quotes)
usmon.reason.rate_limited: Upstream rate limit (429); paused to avoid making it worse
usmon.reason.symbol_missing: Three consecutive no-data answers for the symbol
usmon.reason.yfinance_not_installed: yfinance is not installed; cannot poll (install it and start again)
usmon.err.INVALID_INPUT: Invalid input: interval must be an integer 60–3600 and top N an integer 0–30.

u4.s.title: Does the strategy work across the whole market?
u4.r.title: Stock by stock
u4.x.beat: “Stocks beating buy&hold” = share of stocks where the strategy’s excess Sharpe beats simply holding. Only above 50% does the strategy help overall.
u4.x.half: In-sample = first half, out-of-sample = second half.
u4.x.persist: is the rank correlation, across stocks, of “how much the strategy beats holding” in-sample vs out-of-sample. Near 0 means stocks that did well in-sample do not do better out-of-sample —
u4.x.luck: picking stocks by past backtests is mostly luck.
u4.x.top: “In-sample top 10% → OOS” takes the best 10% of stocks in-sample and shows how they do out-of-sample versus all stocks (grey number).
u4.x.click: Click a row to switch the strategy of the table below.
